bugs.criterion: Announcement bar always contains readable text
bugs.description: On mobile viewport (390x844, matching form_factor=mobile), the persistent data-testid=announcement-message span is present in the DOM with correct text and opacity:1, but is fully hidden (display:none) due to a leftover CSS rule '.announcement span { display: none; }' inside the '@media (max-width: 767px)' block in frontend/src/index.css (line 394). This rule was written for the OLD implementation (before the keyed-remount/opacity-animation removal) and now blanks out the ONLY message span on all mobile widths, so the announcement bar shows no text at all on mobile — directly violating the criterion.
bugs.evidence: Playwright getByTestId('announcement-message').toBeVisible() times out with 'Received: hidden'. Direct evaluate() on the element returns: {"text":"FREE SHIPPING ON ORDERS ABOVE ₹1,299","opacity":"1","display":"none","visibility":"visible","rect":{"width":0,"height":0,...}}. Screenshot (announcement-bar-opacity-never-blank-failure.png) shows the dark-brown bar at the top of the mobile homepage rendered with no visible text. Source: frontend/src/index.css:394 '.announcement span { display: none; }' inside '@media (max-width: 767px)' (lines 392-394), while BrandHeader.tsx:52 renders exactly one persistent '<span class="announcement-message" data-testid="announcement-message">' as described in the briefing — the CSS selector '.announcement span' still matches it and hides it.

action_items.detail: Remove or scope the stale '.announcement span { display: none; }' rule in frontend/src/index.css (~line 394, inside @media (max-width: 767px)) so the persistent .announcement-message span remains visible on mobile.

summary: 2 failed, 0 passed, 0 flaky, 0 blocked, 0 test_error. Both mobile-viewport browser checks for the announcement bar fail: a stale CSS rule '.announcement span { display: none; }' inside the '@media (max-width: 767px)' block (frontend/src/index.css:394) hides the persistent data-testid=announcement-message span entirely on mobile, even though the component itself (BrandHeader.tsx) correctly renders one persistent span with opacity:1 and correct rotating text as described in the briefing. This is a real regression left over from before the keyed-remount/opacity-animation removal, and it directly contradicts both acceptance criteria on the mobile form_factor this app targets. No backend test file was needed (pure client-side CSS/timing criteria, no API surface).
